chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a child who steals.

He said: “If he is seven years old or younger, it is lifted from him. If he repeats it after seven, his fingertip is cut off or scraped until it bleeds. If he repeats it, then what is below his fingertip is cut from him. If he repeats it after that, and he has reached nine years of age, his hand is cut off. And no prescribed limit from the limits of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is to be neglected.”

key_terms.تِسْعَ سِنِينَ: nine years of age, marking a later legal threshold here
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely prescribed legal limits or punishments of Allah
key_terms.سَبْعُ سِنِينَ: seven years of age, marking an initial legal threshold here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a child who steals repeatedly?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a child who commits theft, outlining graduated disciplinary and penal consequences based on age and repeated offense. It emphasizes that the hudud of Allah عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ are not to be neglected, framing the matter within judicial enforcement.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5105 - Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:
I asked Imam (as) about a child who steals.

Imam (as) said: "If he is seven years old or younger, the punishment is lifted from him.
But if he repeats the act after the age of seven, his fingertip is to be cut off or scraped until it bleeds.
If he repeats it again, a part below his fingertip is to be cut off.
If he steals again after that and has reached nine years of age, his hand is to be cut off.
None of the prescribed punishments of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, are to be neglected."
